title: Hungarian Mushroom Soup
subtitle: Rich paprika and dill mushroom soup with soured cream
excerpt: A thick, paprika-spiced mushroom soup from Hungary with dill and soured cream stirred in at the end. It is deeply savoury and ready in under an hour.
sourceNotes: Hungarian home cooking tradition, goulash-spiced mushroom soup variant popular across Central Europe.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the soured cream. Stir in the cream after reheating. Keeps for three months.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well in a large pot. Freeze in portions without the cream.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the base a day ahead without the soured cream. Reheat and stir in the cream just before serving.

content.text: This soup is thick and warming, built around sweet paprika and plenty of mushrooms. The soured cream goes in off the heat so it does not split. Stir it in at the very last moment.
Melt the butter in the large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion with a pinch of salt. Cook for 6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and mushrooms. Cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the mushrooms have released their liquid and it has mostly evaporated.
Stir in the sweet paprika and flour. Cook for 1 minute, stirring constantly, so the flour cooks out.
Pour in the stock gradually, stirring as you go to avoid lumps. Add the milk. Bring to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes. Taste and add the hot paprika if using. Season with salt and pepper.
Remove from the heat. Stir in the soured cream, dill and lemon juice. Do not let the soup boil after this.
Ladle into bowls and serve with crusty bread. Add a small spoonful of extra soured cream on top.

items.cause: The soup was still boiling when the cream was stirred in.
items.fix: The flavour is the same. Next time, take the pan off the heat and wait 30 seconds before adding the cream.

items.cause: The flour was not cooked long enough before the liquid was added.
items.fix: Return to the heat and simmer for a further 10 minutes. The floury taste will cook out.

items.cause: Not enough flour was used, or the stock quantity was too high.
items.fix: Mix 1 tbsp of flour with 2 tbsp of cold water to a paste. Stir into the simmering soup and cook for 5 minutes.
